title: Against Empire
author: Michael Parenti
desc: El imperio estadounidense al desnudo: intervenciones militares, control económico, destrucción de democracias.
tesis: Estados Unidos no es una democracia que ocasionalmente interviene en otros países — es un imperio que utiliza la retórica democrática como cobertura para la dominación global. Parenti documenta cómo el gobierno estadounidense ha derrocado gobiernos electos, armado dictaduras, impuesto ajustes económicos, bombardeado civiles y saqueado recursos naturales en todo el mundo, todo mientras se presenta como defensor de la libertad. El imperialismo no es un error de política exterior sino la lógica inevitable de un capitalismo que necesita mercados cautivos, mano de obra barata y materias primas controladas. La CIA, el Pentágono, el FMI y el Banco Mundial son las herramientas complementarias de un solo proyecto imperial.
ideas: El imperialismo estadounidense no es una serie de 'errores' o 'excesos' — es un sistema racional que sirve a los intereses del capital corporativo.
Las intervenciones militares de EE.UU. siempre van dirigidas contra gobiernos que intentan redistribuir riqueza, nacionalizar recursos o construir soberanía económica.
La 'ayuda exterior' funciona como subsidio a las corporaciones estadounidenses y mecanismo de endeudamiento de los países receptores.
Los medios de comunicación mainstream son parte integral de la maquinaria imperial: fabrican el consentimiento para cada nueva guerra.
La pobreza en el Tercer Mundo no es un 'atraso' sino el producto directo del saqueo imperial — los países son pobres porque son saqueados.
contexto: Publicado en 1995, tras la caída de la URSS, cuando el triunfalismo estadounidense alcanzaba su apogeo con el 'fin de la historia' de Fukuyama. Parenti, politólogo de Yale, llevaba décadas enseñando y escribiendo contra el imperialismo cuando era impopular hacerlo. El libro sintetiza décadas de investigación en un formato accesible y provocador.
porqueLeer: Porque es la demolición más completa y legible del mito del 'excepcionalismo americano'. Parenti escribe con claridad devastadora, sin jerga académica. Cada página tiene datos concretos: intervenciones, cifras, nombres. Es el manual esencial para entender la política exterior de EE.UU.

conexiones.razon: Lenin teorizó el imperialismo como fase del capitalismo; Parenti lo documenta como práctica cotidiana de EE.UU.
Zinn cuenta la historia del imperio desde dentro; Parenti analiza su funcionamiento presente.
Galeano narra el saqueo de América Latina; Parenti explica el mecanismo imperial detrás del saqueo.
Inventing Reality complementa este libro: los medios fabrican el consenso que hace posible el imperio.

deck.label: NotebookLM briefing — The Architecture of Empire

quotes.text: The essence of capitalism is to turn nature into commodities and commodities into capital. The live green earth is transformed into dead gold bricks.

Imperialism has been the most powerful force in world history over the last four or five centuries, carving up whole continents while oppressing indigenous peoples and obliterating entire civilizations. Yet, empire as it exists today is seldom accorded any serious attention by our academics, media commentators, and political leaders.
By 'imperialism' I mean the process whereby the dominant politico-economic interests of one nation expropriate for their own enrichment the land, labor, raw materials, and markets of another people.

Self-sufficient peoples are forcibly transformed into disfranchised wage workers. Indigenous communities and folk cultures are replaced by mass-market, mass-media, consumer societies. Cooperative lands are supplanted by agribusiness factory farms, villages by desolate shanty towns, autonomous regions by centralized autocracies.

tl: Estados Unidos arrebata Puerto Rico a España

Most of what is now the continental United States was forcibly wrested from Native American nations. California and all of the Southwest USA were taken from Mexico by war. Florida and Puerto Rico were seized from Spain.
Ch. Inventing Enemies
Roosevelt arrebata la Zona del Canal de Panamá
One is reminded of Teddy Roosevelt's boast almost a century ago regarding his imperialist intervention in Panama: 'I took the Canal Zone and let Congress debate.'
Ch. Constitutional Tyranny
La tropa explica por qué pelea: tierra y Madero

Sometimes the dollar follows the sword, as when military power creates opportunities for new investments. Thus, in 1915, U.S. leaders, citing 'political instability,' invaded Haiti and crushed the popular militia. The troops stayed for nineteen years. During that period, French, German, and British investors were pushed out and U.S. firms tripled their investments in Haiti.
Ch. Why Intervention?
Quince potencias capitalistas invaden la Rusia soviética

Within a matter of months, the United States and fourteen other capitalist nations invaded Soviet Russia. The U.S. public was told that (1) this military action was to prevent the Bolshevik government from aiding the Germans, with whom the Western allies were still at war.
Ch. Reaching for Pretexts
Hiroshima y Nagasaki: la bomba atomica como mensaje
In regard to nuclear weapons, the United States was the first to develop the atom bomb and the only one ever to use it – at Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945.
Ch. Discouraging Arms Proliferation
Eisenhower desembarca 10,000 marines en Líbano

In 1958, to justify the landing of 10,000 U.S. Marines in Lebanon (sent there to save the procapitalist, comprador government from a nationalist uprising), President Eisenhower claimed that U.S. citizens had to be evacuated to a safer place. In fact, they had been forewarned to avoid travel in Lebanon and most American civilians had departed that country well before the marines arrived.
Ch. Protecting Americans Abroad
Washington derroca a Juan Bosch en Dominicana

In 1962, in the Dominican Republic, after thirty years of the U.S.-supported dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo, a free and fair election brought Juan Bosch to the presidency. Bosch called for land reform, low-rent housing, nationalization of some businesses, public works projects, a reduction in the import of luxury items, and civil liberties for all political groups. Washington held a jaundiced view of Bosch, seeing him as the purveyor of 'creeping socialism.' After only seven months in office, he was overthrown by the U.S.-backed Dominican military.
Ch. Protecting Americans Abroad
Invasión estadounidense a República Dominicana

But when it became apparent that the military junta would be ousted, President Lyndon Johnson sent in U.S. forces 'to protect American lives.' One might wonder why 23,000 troops were needed to rescue a relatively small number of Americans, none of whom were calling for help, some of whom were actually assisting the constitutionalists?
Ch. Protecting Americans Abroad
Golpe en Indonesia: entre medio millón y un millón de muertos

In 1955, the CIA spent $1 million in Indonesia to back a conservative Muslim party, but the party did poorly, while the communists did well. So the CIA set about to negate the election results by backing an armed coup a few years later that failed and another in 1965 that succeeded, costing an estimated 500,000 to one million lives, in what was the worst bloodletting since the Holocaust.
Ch. Elections Yes! (Depending on Who Wins)
Golpe contra Allende en septiembre de 1973

In justifying the overthrow of Chile's democratically elected president, Salvador Allende, in 1973, Henry Kissinger remarked that when we have to chose between the economy and democracy, we must save the economy. Kissinger was uttering a half-truth. It would have been the whole truth if he had said he wanted to save the capitalist economy.
Ch. In the Name of Democracy
Bolivia: el 'Golpe de la Cocaína' instala a la junta militar

In 1980 in Bolivia, the CIA helped overthrow a democratically elected, reformist government and install a rightist military junta. Marked by mass arrests, torture, and killings, the takeover became known as 'the Cocaine Coup' in recognition of how the new rulers openly cooperated with Bolivia's cocaine lords.
Ch. Which Side Are You On, Boys?
Invasión de Granada celebrada como rescate, 1983

In 1983, the familiar refrain of 'American lives in danger' was played again when President Reagan invaded the tiny nation of Grenada (population 102,000), in an unprovoked assault, in violation of international law, killing scores of the island's defenders.
Ch. Protecting Americans Abroad
Elecciones de 1988 y caída del sistema

In Mexico in 1988, the popular left candidate Cuauhtemoc Cárdenas, with a decisive lead in the opinion polls, had the election stolen from him. The government confiscated all the ballots and refused to release the voting results for days. Opposition counters were barred from the tallying.
Ch. Elections Yes! (Depending on Who Wins)
Invasión gringa de Panamá en diciembre de 1989

The White House would have us believe that the purpose of the 1989 invasion of Panama was to apprehend President Manuel Noriega, because he had dealt in drugs and was therefore in violation of U.S. laws. Here the United States operated under the remarkable principle that its domestic laws had jurisdiction over what the heads of foreign nations did in their own countries.
Ch. The 'War On Drugs': Cover Story
Masacre de la Guerra del Golfo contra Iraq

The Iraqi evacuation was turned into a U.S. aerial slaughter of the retreating troops. Over 100,000 Iraqis, including many civilians, were killed in the one-sided conflict. There were a few hundred U.S. casualties.
Ch. Reaching for Pretexts
Wolfowitz redacta la doctrina de hegemonía única

The Pentagon's 'Defense Planning Guidance' draft (1992) urges the United States to continue to dominate the international system by 'discouraging the advanced industrialized nations from challenging out leadership or even aspiring to a larger global or regional role.'
Ch. A Global Military Empire
Bush envía tropas a Somalia para 'aliviar la hambruna'

Just days before he left office in January 1993, President Bush sent troops to Somalia supposedly to safeguard food distribution to its hungry people. Here seemed to be another worthy humanitarian cause.
Ch. Famine Relief for Conoco
Clinton invade Haití y exprime a Aristide

President Clinton eventually imposed economic sanctions on Haiti and in September 1994 invaded and occupied that country with the professed intent of reviving democracy and restoring Aristide to office.
Ch. Operation Facelift
